text:
max: heads up — after yesterday's runtime patch the prefix/KV cache hit-rate fell from ~82% -> ~37% on prod canary. believe root cause is key normalization change in prompt preprocessing. we need a prewarm plan for the full rollout.

anya: ugh. can you paste the perf numbers and the offending diff?

max: yeah quick summary:
- before: global prefix-hit 82%, tail RT mean 42ms token, cost per token baseline
- after (canary): prefix-hit 37%, tail RT spikes +60% for some p99 paths, CPU on host up 20%
- diff: prompt_normalizer now strips unicode variation + canonicalizes whitespace -> changed cache key semantics for ~45% of requests

sam: that matches what I saw in profiling — KV lookup rate halved and batching didn't merge as often because keys diverged. kernel selection unaffected.

daria: we should avoid reverting if possible. options: (1) make normalization backward-compatible for keying, (2) run a deploy-time warmer that re-hashes existing active prefixes, (3) autoscaler hook to run warmers on scale events, (4) scheduled synthetic prewarm job that scrubs hot keys each hour.

eli: +1 to autoscaler hook + a canary warmer. the main risk is cost and hitting rate limits with synthetic traffic. need throttles.

max: proposed immediate plan:
1) quick patch to restore old keying for deployed model variants (rollback key change) — hotfix A (short-term)
2) create deploy-time warmer that replays recent prefix traces onto new key scheme during rollout (medium-term)
3) implement autoscaler warm hook so when new instances spin up they pull last-N hot keys from metadata and run warm calls (long-term)

anya: for (2) how would the deploy-time warmer run? do we have an endpoint?

sam: we can reuse the existing warmers service but need a lightweight replay payload. example curl we used in staging:
```
curl -X POST https://warmers.internal.redwood/v1/warm \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WARMER_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "model": "gptx-13b", "prefixes": ["Hi there","Translate to fr: Hello"] }'
```

max: exact. deploy-time flow: CI creates artifact + a small warm manifest (last 1k hot prefixes) -> deploy controller calls /warm on new instances with rate limit 50 req/s -> instances mark warmed=true for those keys.

daria: and autoscaler hook idea: when node created call `/warm?from=metadata_store&limit=500` so we avoid pulling full traces. also add exponential backoff if warm fails.

eli: also add metric labels: warm_source=(deploy|autoscale|cron), keys_warmed, keys_hit_after_warm, warm_duration_ms. we need dashboards to confirm effectiveness.

anya: schedule approach: run cron every 2 hours to warm top-10k prefixes. cron example: `0 */2 * * *` running warmers in a staggered window to avoid bursts.

sam: caution: synthetic traffic can confuse evals / cost. mark warm requests with header `X-Warm-Job: true` and filter them out of usage billing/quality telemetry.

max: agree. also add TTL on warmed entries (default 6h) and make it configurable per-customer. avoids stale memory.

deploy-bot: created deploy run warmers/1746823501 that will execute warm manifest for canary starting in 10m.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-452: "prewarm/rollback plan for prompt-normalizer key change" and linked to this thread.

anya: next steps I can take: draft PR for deploy-controller to emit warm manifest and add warm header. sam can you draft the warm endpoint throttling + metrics?

sam: on it. I'll add a rate limiter and counters, pushing a small staging change today.

daria: I'll own the cron job and coordinate with Cost to ensure warm runs are budgeted.

eli: I'll add dashboard panels and a regression alert when post-deploy hit-rate < 70% for 15m.

max: thanks. timeline: hotfix for keying tonight, staging warmers validated tomorrow, canary warm-run after staging signoff, then gradual rollout with autoscaler hooks next week. :thumbsup:

anya: SGTM. keep updates here.

sam: FYI found a small edge: some prefixes include ephemeral session tokens — we should scrub personal tokens before warming. I'll add scrub step.

max: excellent. that should reduce noise. posting links: warmers service repo https://git.internal/warmers, infra ticket INF-452, deploy run 1746823501.

anya: thanks everyone.
